questions.prompt: Given that Bacillus, Clostridium, and Clostridioides form endospores resistant to heat and chemicals, which method described in this module is REQUIRED (not just disinfection) to guarantee their destruction?

options.text: Boiling at 100°C for 10 minutes
Autoclaving at 121°C, 15 PSI, for 15 minutes
Regular hand soap
Pasteurization at 72°C for 15 seconds

questions.explanation: Only autoclaving (true sterilization) reliably destroys endospores; boiling and pasteurization only disinfect.

questions.prompt: Which item classification would a stethoscope fall into, and why does this mean it doesn't require sterilization?

options.text: Critical, because it penetrates tissue
Semi-critical, because it touches mucous membranes
Non-critical, because it only contacts unbroken skin
It always requires full sterilization regardless of contact type

questions.explanation: A stethoscope only contacts unbroken skin, placing it in the non-critical category, which needs only routine cleaning.

questions.prompt: Which statement comparing sterilization and disinfection methods is FALSE?

options.text: Boiling water disinfects but does not sterilize, since it doesn't destroy endospores.
Autoclaving can achieve true sterilization.
Pasteurization is intended to sterilize (destroy ALL microbes) in milk.
Dry heat ovens can achieve sterilization, including of endospores.
Ethylene oxide gas can sterilize heat-sensitive items, including killing endospores.

questions.explanation: False — pasteurization is intended to disinfect/reduce microbial load while preserving product quality, not to fully sterilize.

questions.prompt: A hospital needs to sterilize a batch of plastic tubing that would melt or warp under heat. Explain why heat-based methods are ruled out, and identify a suitable alternative from this module, explaining how it works.
questions.explanation: Heat-based sterilization (autoclave, dry heat ovens) would damage or melt heat-sensitive plastic items. Ethylene oxide gas is a suitable alternative — a pressurized gas sterilant capable of killing even endospores without exposing the item to damaging heat or moisture (though it is carcinogenic, requiring careful handling).

questions.prompt: Why is antibacterial hand soap generally NOT recommended over regular soap for routine at-home hand washing?

options.text: Antibacterial soap doesn't kill any bacteria at all
Antibacterial soap's germicidal chemicals need more contact time than a typical ~15-second hand wash provides to actually work
Regular soap is more toxic
Antibacterial soap is a sterilant, so it's too strong for skin

questions.explanation: Antibacterial soap's active ingredients need longer contact time than a routine hand wash provides, so regular soap works just as well at home.

why.A: It does kill bacteria, given enough time.

questions.prompt: Which pair of germicide category and its associated safety concern is correctly matched?

options.text: Alcohols — carcinogenic
Ethylene oxide — carcinogenic
Biguanides — highly toxic, unsafe on any tissue
Peroxides — explosive at all concentrations

questions.explanation: Ethylene oxide's known safety concern is that it's carcinogenic.

why.C: Chlorhexidine is safe enough for mouthwash.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the germicide categories covered in this module is FALSE?

options.text: Alcohols (e.g., isopropyl alcohol) are commonly used as antiseptics.
Biguanides (e.g., chlorhexidine) are common in mouthwash.
Iodine is the MOST effective but also the MOST toxic halogen.
Hydrogen peroxide works best on inanimate objects rather than living tissue.
Ethylene oxide is a pressurized gas capable of killing endospores.

questions.explanation: False — fluorine, not iodine, is the most effective and most toxic halogen; iodine is the LEAST effective but safest, which is why it's used as an antiseptic.

why.D: True — peroxide works best on objects.

questions.prompt: Explain why filtration is often chosen over heat-based methods specifically for sterilizing certain liquids or air, referencing what filtration actually does versus what heat does.
questions.explanation: Filtration physically removes microorganisms by passing liquid or air through a filter with pores smaller than about 0.4 micrometers, without exposing the material to heat at all — ideal for heat-sensitive liquids or air (like HEPA filtration in operating rooms), whereas heat works by denaturing proteins, which would damage a heat-sensitive substance.

questions.prompt: UV radiation and ionizing radiation both control microbial growth by damaging DNA. In which setting is UV radiation specifically noted as useful in this module?

options.text: Deep tissue sterilization inside the body
Surface and air disinfection, such as in operating rooms
Preserving food via freezing
Autoclaving

questions.explanation: UV radiation is used for surface/air disinfection, such as in operating rooms, and for treating food and air.

questions.prompt: Salting, sugaring, refrigeration, and freeze-drying are all preservation methods. Which two work by directly removing or limiting available water, rather than simply slowing metabolism?

options.text: Refrigeration and freeze-drying
Salting/sugaring and freeze-drying
Refrigeration and salting/sugaring
None of them involve water

questions.explanation: Salting/sugaring draws water out via osmosis, and freeze-drying sublimates moisture directly — refrigeration instead slows metabolism without removing water.

why.A: Refrigeration slows metabolism; it doesn't remove water.

questions.prompt: A critical medical item (like a scalpel) is cleaned to a level that only reduces microbes to a "publicly safe" level rather than eliminating all of them. Why would this be inadequate, based on the item classification system?

options.text: Because critical items penetrate tissue and must be completely sterile — nothing less than full sterilization is acceptable
Because scalpels are non-critical and this level would actually be fine
Because sanitization is always stronger than sterilization
Because critical items don't need any cleaning at all

questions.explanation: Critical items (which penetrate tissue) require full sterilization; sanitization alone is not sufficient.

questions.prompt: Compare pasteurization and autoclaving in terms of their goals (sterilize vs. disinfect), and explain why using an autoclave on milk would be inappropriate even though it achieves a "stronger" result.
questions.explanation: Autoclaving achieves true sterilization (121°C, 15 PSI, 15 min) but would cook/ruin milk's taste and quality. Pasteurization (72°C, 15 sec) only disinfects — reducing microbial load enough for safety — while preserving product quality, which is the balance needed for something consumed for taste rather than requiring total sterility.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be the BEST choice to sanitize (not sterilize) dishes at a restaurant, based on the terminology in this module?

options.text: An autoclave
Washing to a level considered safe for public health, not full sterilization
Ethylene oxide gas
UV surface disinfection only

questions.explanation: Sanitization is specifically defined as reducing microbes to a publicly-safe level, which is exactly what restaurant dishwashing aims for.

why.D: UV alone isn't how dishes are sanitized.

questions.prompt: Which statement about critical, semi-critical, and non-critical items is FALSE?

options.text: An endoscope, which touches mucous membranes, is semi-critical.
A needle, which penetrates tissue, is critical.
An exam table, which touches only unbroken skin, is non-critical.
Non-critical items require the same level of sterilization as critical items.
Semi-critical items require high-level disinfection, though not necessarily full sterilization.

questions.explanation: False — non-critical items need only routine cleaning, far less than the full sterilization required for critical items.

why.E: True — semi-critical items need high-level disinfection.

questions.prompt: Why would a hospital use ethylene oxide gas rather than an autoclave for sterilizing linens and pillows?

options.text: Ethylene oxide is cheaper
Autoclaving would damage/be inappropriate for these heat- and moisture-sensitive items, while ethylene oxide gas can sterilize (including endospores) without heat or moisture damage
Ethylene oxide is safer than autoclaving with no safety concerns at all
Linens and pillows cannot be sterilized by any method

questions.explanation: Ethylene oxide gas achieves sterilization without the heat/moisture that would damage linens and pillows.

why.D: They can be sterilized — with ethylene oxide.
